features.title: World Shell navigation to a tracked job opportunity, its linked draft outputs, provenance and the shared editor
features.build: The member journey works entirely from the World Shell (/world) — admin navigation is irrelevant. Member logs in (lands on /world), reaches the career opportunity pipeline from a World Shell island/entry, opens a tracked opportunity (placeholder: company + role title), sees the application-package outputs linked to it (drafts) with provenance proving they came from the member's own Career Master (source, dates, authors, version, lineage). Opens a draft in the EXISTING shared editor (HerqOutputConfigurator / OutputTemplateConfigurator — no new editor), edits, saves (new draft version), Approve for QR through useToolCategoryGate().run and assertReadyToFinalize. UI to create a placeholder opportunity and link/unlink outputs; import-application-package.mjs option to create/link the placeholder from the gitignored package JSON (never hardcode a company or role). Additive storage. Desktop + 390px. Fictional data: 'Northwind Freight', 'Principal Value Architect'.

features.title: Outputs populate from Career Master with per-output overrides; packages enter Career Master via the reconciliation queue
features.build: Career Master is the source of truth ('Career Master + overrides'). Template-driven AND imported outputs bind sections (roles, skills, tools, certifications, KPIs) to Career Master, with per-output overrides stored on the output and shown as overridden in the editor (revert per field). An imported package's differences go to the Career Reconciliation queue — accept writes to Career Master through normal CRUD, reject keeps the override. Queue reachable from the World Shell and the output editor (UI, not API-only). Approve/publish through the finalization gate.

features.title: Cover letter per opportunity, package table of contents, confined cover-letter agent

features.title: World Shell layered navigation: the sun crystal is the root menu and every click moves one layer deeper, with more detail on each object
features.build: Owner direction (2026-10-09): 'the world shell navigation should leverage the sun crystal menu nav and then every click after is the user moving another layer deep … the user moving through layers with more detail exposed against each object in the scene at each layer.' Today (src/components/WorldShell.jsx) the sun core (CRYSTAL_VARIANTS.signature, ~:259) only zooms out on click; islands come from resolveWorldIslands (src/lib/worldIslands.js); deeper levels are ad-hoc React state (focusedKey, atmosphereKey, selectedOpportunityId in useOpportunityPipeline, OpportunityOutputsSection's editor/historyOpen) with a separate '← Back to World' per level, returnKeyRef one level deep, no breadcrumb and no URL state (refresh loses place). Build ONE layer model, reusing what exists (no new 3D scene, no forked crystal variants — crystalGeometry.js rules): 1) Layer 0 = the sun: clicking the sun crystal opens the root menu — the islands presented around the sun as the menu (keyboard/screen-reader accessible list mirrored in the DOM), each labelled. 2) A useWorldLayers stack hook ({kind, key, label} per layer: island → atmosphere/moon or docked panel → item e.g. opportunity → sub-object e.g. output → version/editor) that every existing level pushes to instead of its own state; every click into an object pushes exactly one layer; the camera moves toward the selected object and the panel for that layer shows more detail about that object than the layer above (summary at the layer above, full detail + its child objects as clickable entries at its own layer). 3) A breadcrumb trail (Sun › island › item › sub-object) always visible in the World Shell; clicking a crumb pops to that layer; existing back buttons become 'pop one layer' (keep their labels working so world-shell-navigation's training spec still passes); Escape and browser Back pop one layer. 4) The stack is in the URL (/world?at=...) so refresh, Back/Forward and shared links restore the exact layer; unknown or no-longer-permitted entries fall back to the deepest valid layer with a visible note (never a blank screen). 5) Applies to members and admins, World / Journeys tabs (Journeys cards push the same layers), classic/embed views are layers too. Desktop and 390px (rail becomes a bottom sheet; crumbs wrap or collapse to '… › current' with the full trail one tap away). Reduced motion: camera cuts instead of flights. Training spec journeys must cover: sun menu → island → opportunity → output → version and back out by crumb, Back, Escape; refresh at depth; a deep link; member and admin; 390px. Fictional data only ('Northwind Freight', 'Principal Value Architect'). Change spec traces to docs/changes/world-shell-opportunity-outputs.md v1 and the island registry design in src/lib/worldIslands.js. BREADCRUMBS ARE THE PATH TAKEN (owner, 2026-10-09: 'i also need to be able to navigate back to the summary pages so i need breadcrumbs'): the trail records every layer the user actually passed through, including summary/list pages — the sun menu, the Journeys grid, an island's list view (e.g. the tracked-opportunities list), an outputs list, a version history — so every summary page is a clickable crumb that returns to it with its scroll position and filters intact. Opening the same object from a different summary page yields a different trail. Training spec must include: reach the same opportunity once via the sun menu and once via the Journeys grid and show each trail returns to the summary page it came from.

features.title: Live release tracker inside the Salt Basin platform: real-time trends, history slider, drill-down layers and numbered updates
features.build: Owner direction (2026-10-09): 'i want to rebuild this into my platform for real time updates in the salt basin website itself.' Port the release tracker (reference implementation: tools/release-tracker/index.html — its data rules, layers and validated chart palette are the spec; scripts/release-tracker-sync.mjs, release-history.mjs and release-update.mjs define the data shapes) into the platform as a real, live screen. REUSE FIRST: build on release-intelligence (release_* tables created lazily by releaseIntelligenceSchema.js, releaseLogImporter.js already reads tracker snapshots) and on the in-app release loop's screen if it is merged (never a second parallel release store). 1) INGEST, append-only (every snapshot kept, nothing overwritten, so history replays): (a) push — POST /api/release-tracker/snapshots with a per-release ingest token (generated, shown once, stored hashed, revocable in the UI) carrying the snapshot, history and updates JSON; (b) pull — because the agents' cloud container cannot reach saltbasin.net, the platform also fetches the committed files (docs/release-log/active-release.state.json, history.json, updates.json, active-release.features.json) from the configured public GitHub repo + branch, on a GitHub push webhook (HMAC-verified secret) and on a configurable poll interval as fallback. Repo, branch, interval, webhook secret and tokens are all edited in a Settings tab — no API-only configuration. 2) REAL TIME: a server-sent-events stream (/api/release-tracker/stream) notifies open viewers the moment a new snapshot lands; the client refetches and re-renders without a page reload, shows 'Updated N s ago' and a reconnecting state, and falls back to polling if the stream drops — never a silent stale screen. 3) UI reachable from the World Shell (an island/entry 'Release tracker'), rendered in the Salt Basin design language (brand.css tokens, Fraunces/Jost, light + dark): the overview trends panel (Show: Bugs / Test scores / Features passed; As: Totals / Change per update; Feature filter; legend toggles per series; as-of tiles with change vs previous update; time slider over every recorded state with update markers, prev/next-update and Live; the update note at the slider point; per-feature test-score sparklines; Table view), then the drill-down layers with path breadcrumbs (stat tile → list; feature → rounds, own bugs, backlog, agents; round → stages and bugs; bug → root cause, scope with evidence, history with commit links; agent → result, live test log, failures; status updates list → update detail with comparison). URL holds the path so refresh, Back and shared links restore it. Keep the validated chart colours (light #0B79A8,#B0661A,#9C4A8C,#4A8C2A; dark #2794C9,#C27C28,#B566A6,#6BA642), one axis per chart, hover tooltips, and the Table view. Use an existing chart approach in the repo (src/lib/careerCharts.js SVG helpers) or add chart.js as an npm dependency — not a CDN script. 4) ACCESS, configurable in Settings: admins always; selected members by email (e.g. a partner); optional read-only share link with a revocable token. Default admin-only. Bug/agent text shown to non-admin viewers is the same counts/labels-only data the snapshot already limits itself to. 5) The Claude Code side: extend scripts/release-tracker-sync.mjs (or a small companion script) with an optional push to the platform when PLATFORM_URL + an ingest token are set, logging (never hiding) a failed push. Training journeys must cover: ingest by pull with a fictional fixture repo state and by push with a token; a second ingest arriving while the screen is open updates it live without reload (SSE); slider back to an earlier state and Live; each toggle/filter; drill-down and breadcrumbs back to a summary page; access denied for a member not granted; share link view; revoked token rejected; 390px and dark mode. Fictional data only; this repo is public. WORLD VIEW (owner, 2026-10-09: 'turn this into something accessible through a 3d interactive experience using salt basin 3d objects', as a prototype to extend to other data): a Board / World toggle; World renders the same data as a crystal world built ONLY from src/lib/crystalGeometry.js (addCrystalLights, CRYSTAL_VARIANTS.signature as the release sun, buildGemMesh for features and bug satellites, buildRiverParticles for features with a running agent, projectToScreen for labels) — never forked geometry. Encoding (from the reference tools/release-tracker/index.html): crystal colour = feature status (legend in the panel), size = test steps, gold ring arc = share of steps passing, satellites = bugs coloured by the chart series (open / verified / backlog / waiting on a person), light river = agent working now. Drag to orbit, wheel/pinch to zoom, hover tooltip, click a crystal to fly in and open the same drill-down layer in a side panel (bottom sheet at 390px), breadcrumbs and URL shared with the Board, history slider replays the world at any recorded moment, reduced motion = camera cuts and no spin, a DOM list of every crystal for keyboard/screen-reader users, phone hides crowded labels. Build it as a reusable engine: a generic graph contract (root + nodes { id, label, sub, status, statusLabel, weight, progress, active, href, satellites[] }) and a release-tracker adapter, so other worlds (opportunities, Career Master, outputs) only add adapters. Training journeys cover World mode at desktop and 390px, light and dark, fly-in and back by crumb, slider replay. ENVIRONMENT (owner, 2026-10-09: 'make it an underwater scene'): the World is drawn in a swappable environment module, default UNDERWATER (reference: underwaterEnv in tools/release-tracker/index.html) — depth-gradient water with exponential fog, a sea-tinted sand seabed fading into the blue, moving cellular caustics on the sand, swaying light shafts from the surface, rising bubbles and drifting marine snow, kelp anchored outside the camera's orbit so it never crosses a crystal, crystals bobbing gently, white edge lines on crystals for separation from the water, and 'agent working' shown as a stream of bubbles from the centre. Light and dark water palettes; reduced motion stills the water. Add the environment to crystalGeometry.js's family (an environment builder alongside addCrystalLights) rather than a component-local fork. RENDER BINDINGS (owner, 2026-10-09): the tracker's Board and World draw ONLY through render bindings (docs/changes/render-bindings.md, feature render-bindings) — every visual channel mapped to a Port field with transform, legend and change policy; Data map panel per object; pending (approval-required) changes drawn as ghosts with an impact list. If render-bindings is not merged yet when this builds, implement the tracker's bindings through a local registry with the same contract so it swaps to the shared one without changing the renderer.

features.title: Render bindings: every rendering is a view over mapped source data, updated live or through approval with impact analysis
features.build: Build exactly the design in docs/changes/render-bindings.md (read it first; it includes the reuse-first audit — no new tables). Sources are L1 Ports (data_ports / port_source_objects / port_source_fields) with port_type platform_table | connector | calculation | manual; bound values and provenance in journey_rod_evidence (+ additive columns status, proposed_by, decided_by, decided_at); events in journey_rod_events (value_changed, change_proposed, change_approved, change_rejected, writeback_failed); approval steps in agent_approval_workflows (pipeline 'data_change'); calculations via server/lib/metricIntelligence.js variables; bindings in server/lib/renderBindingRegistry.js (code registry + org/member override seam like currentRegistry.js). Deliver: the binding registry and resolver (renderer receives only bound values, unbound = 'not mapped'); a live path (event + SSE fan-out) and an approval path (proposal → steps → approve/reject, ghost rendering of the proposed value, nothing overwritten); impact analysis computed on demand (bindings reading the field, metrics whose variables include it, Tributary-connected rods), snapshot stored on the change_proposed event; enforcement of port_source_fields.editable_roles; a 'Data map' panel for any rendered object and a 'Pending changes' queue screen reachable from the World Shell (prototype: tools/release-tracker/index.html BINDINGS, dataMapTable, pendingSection). First consumer: the release tracker (a platform_table Port describing the release_* tables, data not moved). Fictional data in specs.

features.title: Platform MCP server: every capability usable by AI agents through MCP, with the same permissions as the website and API, plus a parity map
features.build: Owner direction (2026-10-09): 'make sure the user interface is accessible not just through APIs but also through MCP and platform interface through my website'. Build the Salt Basin MCP server inside the Express app using the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (Streamable HTTP transport at /mcp). AUTH: the caller acts as a real platform user — personal access tokens a user creates, names, scopes and revokes in a 'Connected agents' screen reachable from the World Shell (stored hashed; shown once), and the same requireAuth / role / entitlement checks the API applies (never a privileged bypass). REGISTRY: server/lib/mcpToolRegistry.js — append-only (like the block REGISTRY): each tool { name, title, description, inputSchema, permission, handler } whose handler calls the SAME server/lib function the matching API route calls; tools are never removed or renamed once shipped. Seed tools for the capabilities that exist on the branch today, each mirroring an existing route: Career Master read; career opportunities list/create/open; application outputs list/open/new draft version; approve-for-QR through assertReadyToFinalize (respecting the same gates); cover-letter agent turn; release tracker read (and render-binding data map + pending changes when those exist). Tool calls are tracked through usageTracking.js / SALT_BASIN_TRACKED_INTERACTIONS (reuse, no new analytics table) and failures are returned as MCP errors, never swallowed. PARITY MAP: a config registry (server/lib/capabilityParity.js, no table) listing every capability with its UI path (World Shell route), API route and MCP tool name; a 'Capabilities' screen from the World Shell (admin) shows the map with gaps highlighted, and a check script (scripts/check-interface-parity.mjs) that fails CI-style when a registered API route has no UI path or MCP tool. Training journeys: create a token in the UI (desktop and 390px), connect with an MCP client (the validator uses @modelcontextprotocol/sdk Client over Streamable HTTP) and list tools, call a read tool and see the same data as the UI, call a write tool and see the change appear in the UI, a member without permission gets an MCP error, a revoked token is rejected, the Capabilities screen shows parity and gaps. Fictional data only.
